title: Completed perfect scalar models under arbitrary pullback
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and put $A_n=R/\pi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:V'\to V$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $T=V,V'$ put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $\underline M_T$ denote the constant sheaf of an $R$-module $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of finite projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], with specified differential, and set $C_T(P)=B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T$. These are regarded as objects of the ambient derived categories of $B_T$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $Lg^*$ be the specified strict reduction-tower derived pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], equivalently completed pullback on these derived-complete objects [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

There are natural isomorphisms
$$C_T(P)\otimes^L_{B_T}(A_n)_T\cong(A_n)_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T,$$
$$Lg^*C_V(P)\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n\bigl((A_n)_{V'}\otimes_{\underline R_{V'}}\underline{P^\bullet}_{V'}\bigr)\cong C_{V'}(P).$$
The latter identifies all derived-limit projections with the ordinary quotient maps on the displayed bounded complex. Its finite reductions are induced by the canonical constant-section coefficient maps and preserve the given scalar differentials; they commute with consecutive quotient transitions. The comparisons are natural in chain maps of bounded finite-projective complexes.

For every integer $j$, with $N^j=H^j(P^\bullet)$, the canonical comparison for the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] is
$$\mathcal H^j(C_T(P))\cong B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{N^j}_T.$$
Ordinary ringed pullback $g^*=g^{-1}(-)\otimes_{g^{-1}B_V}B_{V'}$ along the projection-induced coefficient map, with $g^{-1}$ the pro-etale inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], of this latter sheaf is canonically $B_{V'}\otimes_{\underline R_{V'}}\underline{N^j}_{V'}$: on balanced tensors the isomorphism sends $b'\otimes(b\otimes n)$ to $b'g^\sharp(b)\otimes n$, with inverse $b'\otimes n\mapsto b'\otimes(1\otimes n)$. Consequently, for any integers $a\le b$, vanishing of $\mathcal H^j(C_V(P))$ for $j\notin[a,b]$ implies the same vanishing for $C_{V'}(P)$. No flatness of $B_{V'}$ over $g^{-1}B_V$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the adic scalar flat-reduction lemma to $T=V,V\prime$. It verifies the coefficient datum and identifies its actual projections; its K-flat representatives and normalized maps give the first displayed derived isomorphism, including differentials, quotient units, transitions and chain-map naturality.

proof.text: Apply the projective quotient-augmentation lemma on both schemes. Its normalized augmentation is invertible, its projections are the ordinary quotient maps, and both scalar models are derived complete. The strict constant-complex base-change lemma identifies the entire finite pullback tower with $(D_{V\prime,n})_n$, with all its differentials and units.

proof.text: Compute the specified integral pullback on the K-flat representative from step 1. By its definition and the strict tower isomorphism of step 2, it is $R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{V\prime,n}$. Invert the target quotient-augmentation isomorphism of step 2 to obtain $C_{V\prime}(P)$; the recorded projection equalities give exactly its quotient maps. The integral/completed comparison applies because the input is derived complete. Its statement identifies the projections of both pullbacks. Every comparison is natural in chain maps: the defining strict derived-limit functor carries the commuting tower squares to commuting squares.

proof.text: Apply exact completed scalar realization with $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $I=(\pi)$; Noetherianity was checked in step 1. It gives the canonical cohomology isomorphism for every $j$. Apply its ordinary balanced-pullback isomorphism to $N=H^j(P)$, which need not be projective. Its two formulas are precisely those asserted, and require no flatness of the projection-induced coefficient map.
